walkthrough: Goal: draw details at a comfortable zoom and angle, step back to see the whole picture, and take strokes back without reaching for a button; start a new artwork of the size I want.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library: a blank white canvas the size of the screen's canvas area sits centred in the dark surround with a margin all round (fit). Draw a wave with the pen: the ink lands under the tip.

Spread two fingers on the canvas: the canvas zooms in about the point between them; a quiet line under the top bar reads the zoom and turn (for example 250 % · 0°) and fades a moment after the fingers lift. Fingers resting still, or a slight wobble, move nothing: pan, zoom and rotation each start only past their own dead zone, and a pinch does not turn the canvas by accident.
Twist the two fingers: the canvas turns with them, about the point between them. Draw a short stroke with the pen at this zoom and angle: it lands exactly under the tip.
Move both fingers together: the canvas pans. Drag one finger across open canvas: it pans too; a finger never draws.

Tap the canvas with two fingers: the last stroke goes, as the side bar's undo would. Tap with three fingers: it comes back, as redo would. A tap starting on the side bar or a panel is no shortcut; fingers that moved are no tap.
Pinch quickly inwards: the whole canvas fits the screen again, upright and centred.

While the pen draws, the side bar's undo and redo look exactly as before the pen landed; a tap on them then would be refused without any change on screen. They grey out only when there is nothing to undo or redo.

Tap Gallery, then the plus: a small panel, New canvas, lists Screen size 2880 × 1716, Square 2048 × 2048, A4 portrait 2480 × 3508 and A4 landscape 3508 × 2480. A tap outside closes it without doing anything else. Tap the plus and Square: a square white canvas opens at fit.
Leave the app and let the system close it, then open it again: the square artwork reopens at fit (the view is not stored). Rotating the tablet refits the canvas to the new shape at the same zoom.

Failure and cancel: a gesture that a third finger, a palm (the pen landing) or a control interrupts does nothing more until every finger lifts. Not here: rotation snapping, the four-finger tap that hides the interface, remembering the view per artwork, touch-and-hold eyedropper.
